messages:
jess: Heads-up: cost dashboard shows cache savings flipping between routes for long-lived sessions that cross billing windows. Looks like credits are getting reassigned at window boundaries. Anyone seen this in prod or staging?

sam: I noticed similar yesterday in staging after the prefetch change. savings jump when session spans slabs.

miho: Are we still using fixed minute slabs for amortization? I thought we had a sliding-window experiment.

jess: Dashboard reads econ API which returns credits grouped by `billing_window_start` (fixed minute slabs).

marta: Repro: start session at :58, prefetch tokens counted in slab N, subsequent hits fall into slab N+1 -> net saving moves to different route in daily rollups.

luke: Two quick ideas: 1) attribute all prefetched credits to the session owner slab until session close; 2) add an annotation field so UI can show both raw slab attribution and session-attributed view.

miho: Option 1 changes the invariants our billing reports rely on (deterministic slab-based invoices). We need monotonicity for accounting.

sam: Option 2 sounds safer: backend emits `carryover_tag` per row that marks hits that logically belong to a previous slab. UI can decide how to present. Minimal change server-side.

jess: Agreed — we should avoid changing invoice semantics. Let's prototype `carryover_tag` boolean that marks session-hit rows.

marta: For the UI, we can show two columns: "raw_slab" and "session_attributed" and an explanatory tooltip. I'll mock in Figma.

miho: Performance note: creating session-grouped aggregates for long sessions could be expensive. We should benchmark query cost and memory if we add session-group grouping to the econ read path.

sam: I'll draft a small API example payload and a PR sketch: `{ "slab_start": 2024,..., "prefetch_tokens": 123, "hit_tokens": 98, "carryover_tag": true }`

marta: SQL I ran (current):
```sql
SELECT slab_start, route_id, SUM(prefetch) prefetch, SUM(hit) hits
FROM econ_prefetch_agg
WHERE slab_start >= :start AND slab_start < :end
GROUP BY slab_start, route_id;
```
This is why attribution flips at the slab boundary.

luke: For a hybrid approach: keep current slab grouping but emit a sampled session map that links session_id -> preferred_slab. UI can use the sample to estimate session carryover impact with bounded cost.

miho: Sampling might be the practical win. Run a 7-day sim with 1% session sample and compare deviation. If errors are within 0.5% we can ship sampling first.

deploy-bot: infra: econ-prefetch-schema migration queued to staging in ~8m: https://deploys.internal/redwood/5678

jess: Plan: (A) sam builds proto API with `carryover_tag` and example responses, (B) miho runs sampling/perf sim and posts results, (C) marta creates UI mock with both columns and tooltip, (D) luke experiments with sampled session-map export. Sync TOMORROW 11am. @sam @miho @marta @luke

sam: will open PR today with payload + test vectors.

miho: starting perf sim now, will share numbers here.

marta: dropping Figma link in #design after mock ready. :sparkles:
